items.title: As the US Treasury suffers a cybersecurity breach, its chief tech guy is vibecoding a Civilization clone
items.summary:
This week, amidst ongoing service disruptions, the US Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed that it is "investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems." The bureau, which collects and analyzes transaction data to combat financial crimes, says it has taken some of its e-filing systems offline "as a proactive measure."

FinCEN hasn't provided an estimate of when the investigation and system disruptions will be resolved, leaving the ability of financial institutions to report suspicious activity and interface with law enforcement indefinitely hampered. Meanwhile, as FinCEN is putting out fires, US Treasury chief information officer Sam Corcos has been busying himself with a different kind of work: He's been vibecoding a Civilization clone.

(Image credit: FinCEN) Corcos' LLM-powered game project was noticed by Bulwark economics editor Catherine Rampell: "The Treasury CIO appears to have spent the past three days vibecoding a Civilization game clone instead of working on this major Treasury database cyber breach," she wrote in a post on X . "As I type this, his Claude code is literally adding theme music."

A DOGE appointee who previously raised cybersecurity concerns at the IRS with an API "hackathon" and sought to cancel engineering efforts intended to modernize its systems, Corcos is hosting his little LLM project on Github. It's called Legatum, and he describes it as "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization."

As Corcos writes in its readme,…

items.title: One of GTA 6's Best Features Was Actually Planned for GTA: Vice City, Reveals Ex-Rockstar Dev
items.summary:
GTA 6's headphones mechanic was originally planned to be included in the original GTA: Vice City, according to a former Rockstar Games employee.

Ex-Rockstar Games dev Obbe Vermeji revealed that the headphones feature was cut from GTA: Vice City due to a technical reason, and they had even created an icon for it. It's unclear what the technical reason was, but Vice City's version likely would've come in the form of a Walkman or cassette player, given it was set in the 80s. GTA 6's version, however, comes with a smartphone and a pair of AirPods.

The feature is pretty incredible, because you can listen to music and podcasts wherever you go. You no longer have to sit in the car to finish a song; you can just get out, put your headphones in, and turn on the radio station you were just listening to. And when combined with combat encounters, it can have some thrilling results. Last night, In the Air Tonight came on as I approached a gang hideout, creating an incredibly cinematic moment for me.

This is the best game ever made dude https://t.co/AFR2jmo0fF

— Cade Onder (@Cade_Onder) November 25, 2026 

It doesn't always have to lead to some epic moment, though. It's great for working out in-game, learning about the world and lore of GTA via podcasts and talk shows, and much more. A lot of effort has been packed into creating GTA 6's in-game media, and the headphones allow you to make full use of it. The only downside is that you can't make any kind of custom playlists. Presumably, this is because Rockstar wants players to organically discover music from the radio stations…

items.title: This GTA 6 Radio Station Represents Its Florida-Inspired Setting Perfectly
items.summary:
Radio stations have always been a staple of Grand Theft Auto, filled with licensed (and some original) songs alongside crazy-ass talk shows. GTA 6 is unprecedented in this field, with its massive tracklist and over-the-top on-air personalities. But we all have the music genres we gravitate towards when picking out a station, and the one I'm rarely ever changing is Dirty South Classics – basically a playlist of the Southern hip-hop bangers I grew up listening to. It's also a thematic fit for GTA 6's setting of Leonida, an obvious parallel to the state of Florida.

While you traditionally wouldn't consider South Florida or the city of Miami part of the American South, the rest of Florida is largely culturally aligned with the region's states like Georgia, Mississippi, and parts of Texas (namely Houston). These are key distinctions to make in the context of music, especially what we consider Southern hip-hop – colloquially known as 'dirty south' hip-hop, hence the station name. Deep bass, rattling hi-hats, catchy melodies with instrumentals that either align with aggressive trap beats or the more soulful funk; characteristics of the genre that you hear throughout Dirty South Classics.

Because of its importance as a subgenre, and as a prominent cultural touchstone of the region that GTA 6 is trying to portray, it got its own dedicated station separate from VCRR, which is for more contemporary rap hits. items.title: AI kills another coding competition: 'I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models'
items.summary:
The Atari Homebrew Awards , an annual celebration of new games developed for old systems by the people who love them both, has been cancelled after eight years of operation—and yes, it's because of AI.

"As you may know, the landscape of retro game development changed dramatically this year with the massively increased capabilities of LLMs. More and more games have incorporated AI elements into their development chain and now have the capability to create full games without writing a single line of code," Atari Homebrew Awards host James, aka ZeroPage Homebrew, wrote on the Atari Age forums .

"Keeping up with the large number of AI-assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on, with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI. This flood of new AI games forced me to re-evaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.

"The Atari Homebrew Awards were now challenged to make sure the work of human developers were still honoured amongst the new fully computer-coded games. I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I quickly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought."

James said he discovered last week that "a large majority" of developers were using AI in some capacity to make their games, from testing to wholesale game creation, "without one typed line of code." And first place went to four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen, not exactly very surprising given his history with the track. items.title: Analyst estimates Call of Duty lost 44% of its players when GTA 6 came out, and unlike fans of its live-service competitors they've been slow to come back
items.summary:
Sony has been crowing about Grand Theft Auto 6 setting a new record for concurrent PlayStation players , which isn't bad for a game that's currently only singleplayer. It isn't just beating the records set by the giants of multiplayer gaming back when they released, though. It's also eating their lunch right now.

Alinea Analytics reports that Call of Duty, Fortnite, and EA Sports FC 27 all saw their number of daily active users drop when GTA 6 released. "Call of Duty got it the worst of the three," Alinea's head of market analysis Rhys Elliott wrote, "dropping 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M" according to the company's estimates.

Fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims, with an estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend, and EA Sports FC 27 suffered a similar loss. "FC 27's DAUs dropped by about 27% when GTA 6 launched," according to Elliott, "from 5.9M to 4.3M."

But where player numbers for both of those games were trending back up four days after GTA 6's release, Call of Duty has struggled to win its players back, Elliott says: "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline."

During that time Call of Duty had a Thanksgiving-themed event, while FC 27 had a Black Friday discount and in-game "Thunderstruck" promotion, and Fortnite's ongoing Treasure Hunters event is adding a bunch of One Piece stuff. If you're going up against a cultural juggernaut like GTA, I guess crossing over with something as massive as One Piece…

items.title: Nvidia patch finally eradicates the SSD-hammering bug its last hotfix didn't actually fix
items.summary:
Nvidia's latest GeForce Game Ready driver, version 621.40 , is out now. "This new Game Ready Driver provides the best gaming experience for Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, and Assetto Corsa Rally," the notes say, "and the addition of DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering to Where Winds Meet."

Which is kind of burying the lead. This patch is really a hotfix for a hotfix, an update that finally addresses the bug with previous driver packages that had them pointlessly rewriting a log file over and over, quickly adding up to tens of GB every hour and potentially damaging SSDs nobody can afford to replace any more.

Over the weekend Nvidia released a hotfix that supposedly caught the bug, only for users to discover it merely delayed its onset . Rather than setting in immediately after a reboot, it would wait until your PC had been on for a while before shitting the bed. If you're one of the people who leaves your computer running overnight then I hope you stayed on version 621.01, the last safe driver package before the current one.

Forum users have been testing out version 621.40 and it seems to have not only stopped the Nvidia container service from freaking out and rewriting its log, but also caught a bug with custom cursors that would make them turn gray. Which is nice. 

I'm tempted to play it safe and stay on my old driver anyway, though I'll update for Dawn of War 4, which comes out on December 3. Ocelot Bloodless Jugular location Head to Belville : It's a town in Leonard County, in the central eastern part of the map, a bit south of Lake Leonida and north of La Perle.

In the northern edge of Belville there's a little cluster of four homes laid out almost in an X pattern. The southernmost home of that cluster has a garage you can break into. Once you open the garage door, you'll see the white Ocelot Bloodless Jugular.

You'll need the key cloner to get in, which I assume you already have since you're doing jobs for Randy. No need to worry about the tracker , it's a standard one so it won't transmit your location to the cops. You still don't want to dawdle, because the owner of the car has a gun and he's not afraid to use it. He'll start shooting if he sees you boost the car.

Randy will pay you $10,615 for the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular. He'll pay an extra $5,000 if you bring it to him in pristine condition.

items.summary:
Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy said at the time. 

"That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good."

But like so many other ambitious new studios launched around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it said was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain."

(Image credit: Gravity Well) A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS ) says the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation."

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. I had plenty of questions when BioWare announced Mass Effect 5 was gonna be a thing though. Could you really write a Mass Effect story in the radically changed galaxy we were left with at the end of Shepard's adventure? Apparently, you could. In a recent AMA on Reddit (via IGN ), BioWare writer Cat Valente wrote that the now-cancelled Mass Effect sequel's team put a lot of work into handling ME3's endings "in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off, [or] at least not piss them off completely".

The goal, says Valente, was to write a continuation of Mass Effect's narrative that "wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another". That tracks with what we've heard before: leaks have suggested ME5 was set to more or less wrap all the previous game's endings into one (Deus Ex: Invisible War style, hell yeah).

"Not for nothing, guys, but that's *kind of a tall fucking order*.
